THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  215

Acceptance of Building:
    On behalf of the founders:
        Mrs. Annie Halsell Woodward, Durant, Okla.
    On behalf of the sponsors:
        Mr. J. Wesley Moulton, Superintendent of Schools, Savoy


DEDICATION OF SAVOY GYMNASIUM

WPA PROJECTS 5023 AND 9708

By Gus W. Thomasson, Administrative Field Officer, Works Progress Administration, Dallas Area

    Mr. Chairman, Ladies, and Gentlemen:

    It has been my good fortune as the Works Progress Administration, when requested so to do by sponsors, to dedicate its major projects, for many purposes. In the course of that duty, I have attended many dedications, but I have considered not only a major but an outstanding major project.


HISTORY OF THE PROJECT

    This project was originally started on May 17, 1937, estimated at that time to cost $16,417.65, of which the Government was to pay $13,364.52, and Savoy Independent School District, as sponsor, was to pay $4,051.13. This period of operation was allocated for 106 workers, 94 unskilled and 12 skilled. Various changes in the project due to some delays in materials due principally to bad weather conditions, plus an increased cost by increased wage scale effective October 1, 1937, and additional work ordered by WPA to complete the project, caused a suspension of operations on February 15, 1938, at which time a supplemental project was submitted to Washington. It was not until May 11, 1938, that the total approval of the new project was finally obtained. The new project as approved and put into a complete place called for an additional outlay of funds of $15,549.52, making a total of $31,997.27, of which the Government agreed to supply $30,063.61 (61.8¢) and the sponsor agreed to supply $11,539.35 (38.2¢).

    On September 19, 1937, the cornerstone of this building was laid with appropriate ceremonies, at which a group of citizens who were students and supporters of this college, and whose names were placed in the stone, and a number of other honored out-of-tellers, their friends and interested parties, attended. The number of number of persons present being estimated as 500 to 600.
